title: Safe refactoring moves
idea: Refactoring changes the structure of code without changing its behaviour, in small named steps, each checked by tests before the next.
points: First pin today's behaviour with tests, even where that behaviour looks odd.
Make one small move at a time: rename, extract, inline or move.
Run the tests after every move, so a mistake points at one change.
Never mix a refactor with a behaviour change in the same step.

hero.title: Cleaning a pricing method, move by move

items.label: Pin behaviour
items.text: Write tests that record what `price` returns today for every seat, age and day.

items.label: Rename
items.text: Replace `t`, `a` and `w` with names that say what they hold.

items.label: Extract constant
items.text: Turn magic numbers such as 300 and 200 into named constants.

items.label: Extract method
items.text: Move the child rule into `discount(age)`; its two copies become one.

items.label: Replace type code
items.text: Swap the `"S"` and `"P"` strings for a `Seat` enum with base prices.

items.label: Compare and commit
items.text: Old and new agree on every pinned case: commit, then find the next smell.

code.title: Before and after, side by side
code.caption: The legacy method and its refactored version run on every valid input mix. Matching results show the behaviour is unchanged for those cases.

walk.text: Before: cryptic names, magic numbers, and the same rules written twice.
Replace type code: each `Seat` carries its base price. Unknown codes, which legacy priced at 0, now throw.
Extract constant: each number gets a name that explains it.
Extract method: the child rule lives in one named place.
A characterization test: run old and new on every case and count matches.
Print the match count, then one sample from the new code.

pitfalls: Do not refactor code with no tests; write characterization tests first.
Keep each commit to one move, so a review or revert stays small.
Stop when the code is clear enough for the next change, not perfect.

quiz.q: Using the refactored code, what does this print?
quiz.why: Base 800, minus the 300 child discount because 11 is under 12, plus the 200 weekend surcharge.

takeaway: Pin the behaviour, make one small move, rerun tests, repeat.
